item: local-ai: make every AI feature run on a local (on-device) model by default (reviewed and corrected)
currentBehaviour:
REVIEWER NOTE: I re-opened every cited file. Most citations hold. Corrections are marked [FIX] and new findings [NEW]. The main new finding is a real, proven bug: every on-device failure is shown as "No Internet Connection" (see below).

There are four LLM features. All of them reach the model through one string-in, string-out path: PixlNet's `AiOrchestrator` (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/AI/AiClients.swift:193-340), built in `AIService.init` (App/Services/AI/AIService.swift:35-62).

WHAT USES AI (call sites):

1. **AI playlist sheet (Daily Mix sparkle) and AI Playlist Lab.**
   - `AIPlaylistController.runGeneration` (App/Features/AI/AIPlaylistController.swift:75-127) calls `AiPlaylistGenerator.generate` (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/AI/AiPlaylist.swift:329-347). The generate call is at :92-95, type .playlist; candidateLimit 120 is at :89.
   - The Lab builds its request text in App/Features/AI/AiPlaylistLabView.swift (`prompt` :282-298) and allows 5-150 songs (`validated()` :301-307).
   - The Daily Mix sparkle (App/Features/Mixes/MixScreens.swift:200-205) is NOT gated on provider status. Only Library's "With AI" is gated.

2. **AI Daily Mix refine.** `refineDailyMix` (AIPlaylistController.swift:134-165) uses type .dailyMix, with minLength max(60% of current, 10) and maxLength max(current size, 20).

3. **TAIS DJ / Taizo chat.** `TaisDjEngine.respond` (App/Services/AI/TaisDjEngine.swift:42-62).
   - A play, queue or find request goes through the deterministic `TaisIntentParser` and `TaisMediaRouter` (same file, :91-182; no AI), plus an AI intro line with a 1.2 s budget (:37, :65-76).
   - Anything else becomes a `.taizoChat` question with a 25 s budget (:36, :48-55).
   - Every message is a fresh, single-turn call with no memory (App/Features/AI/TaisChatModel.swift:83-86).
   - [NEW] The composer lets the user send while a reply is in flight: `canSend` only checks the text (App/Features/AI/TaisChatSheet.swift:206, :230). Requests can therefore overlap.

4. **"Translate via AI"** in the lyrics More sheet.
   - Path: App/Features/Lyrics/LyricsMoreSheet.swift:100-104 → App/Features/Lyrics/LyricsView.swift:373-375 → [FIX path] App/Services/LyricsController.swift:238-258.
   - It calls `AILyricsTranslator.translate` (App/Services/AI/AILyricsTranslator.swift:18-33). The whole LRC goes into one `.general` prompt (:37-59). The reply must echo every line plus its translation with timestamps, and is then validated as LRC (:61-68).
   - A failure message containing "key" or "config" becomes `.notConfigured` (:71-75).

5. **Not ported yet: Android's AI home greeting and expanded insight** (PixlAudio app/src/main/java/com/theveloper/pixelplay/presentation/viewmodel/HomeGreetingStateHolder.kt:68-107 expandInsight and :115-166 refresh, type GREETING).
   - iOS shows only the local fallback (App/Features/Home/HomeStore.swift:9-12, HomeLogic.swift:71-79).
   - Its cache keys exist but nothing reads them (App/Stores/SettingsStore.swift:82-83).

These are not LLMs and are already local:
- TAIS lyric sync (wav2vec2) and instrumentals (MDX) run on Core ML and download on demand (App/Services/ML/ModelCatalog.swift:34-55, ModelManager.swift:249, .github/workflows/ml-convert.yml).
- [NEW] The BS-RoFormer cloud separator is opt-in. It needs a base URL in Developer › Experimental (default "": SettingsStore.swift:728; guard at App/Services/ML/TaisStudio.swift:466-468), so it stays as is.
- Music intelligence is an algorithm.
- "Translate on device" already uses the Translation framework: `.translationTask` at LyricsView.swift:219-226, configuration at :428, and `LyricsTranslator` at :557-579. [NEW] `startTranslation` returns silently when there are no synced lines (:423).

HOW THE PROVIDER IS CHOSEN:
- **The default is Gemini in three places:**
  - `AISettings.provider` default "GEMINI" (SettingsStore.swift:618);
  - `AISettingsBridge.selectedProvider` (App/Services/AI/AISettingsBridge.swift:22-24);
  - `AiProvider.fromString`, which falls back to .gemini (AiProvider.swift:54; pinned by Tests/PixlNetTests/AiTests.swift:51).
- **What `AiOrchestrator.generateContent` (AiClients.swift:236-286) does:**
  - builds the layered system prompt (AiPromptEngine.swift:32-52);
  - checks a 30-minute cache;
  - walks `AiProviderSupport.buildProviderChain(primary)` (AiProvider.swift:142-148). The chain is the primary, then the 11 preferred fallbacks, then ON_DEVICE when it isn't the primary. Any provider with a key, and Ollama, which needs no key, is tried. So choosing on-device still falls back to the cloud;
  - applies a 60 s timeout per call (:196, :314-324).
- [NEW] **The reverse also holds:** with the default Gemini and no key, the chain still ends at ON_DEVICE, after Gemini and the others fail with "no API key" and Ollama fails on its blank URL (AiClients.swift:142-145). So on an Apple Intelligence iPhone the Daily Mix sparkle and "Translate via AI" already reach the on-device model today as a last resort.
- **When every provider fails,** `failureMessage` (:289-298) lists every provider it tried.

[NEW, proven bug] Every on-device failure is shown as "No Internet Connection":
- `OnDeviceAiClient.error` builds its error with `providerName: AiProvider.onDevice.displayName` = "On-Device (Offline)" (OnDeviceAiClient.swift:50-53; AiProvider.swift:40), so every message starts "On-Device (Offline) API error: …".
- `AiPlaylistPrompt.detailedErrorMessage` checks has("offline") before anything on-device-specific (AiPlaylist.swift:290-291) and returns "No Internet Connection…". `resolveErrorMessage` then matches "connect" (AIPlaylistController.swift:252-253).
- So too-long, guardrail, model-not-ready and unsupported-language failures all show "No Internet Connection" on the playlist and Daily Mix paths. Adding rows to `resolveErrorMessage` alone can't fix this, because the text is already gone by the time it gets there.

The on-device provider is `OnDeviceAiClient` (App/Services/AI/OnDeviceAiClient.swift):
- `isAvailable` only checks `SystemLanguageModel.default.availability` (:16-19).
- Each call creates a fresh `LanguageModelSession(instructions:)` with default guardrails (:27). It is never prewarmed and never streams.
- Options are `GenerationOptions(sampling: nil, temperature, maximumResponseTokens 256…4096)` (:28-29). With the default maxTokens of 4096, that output cap equals the whole context window.
- Playlist mode is detected by searching the system prompt for "Return ONLY a raw JSON array of song IDs." (`AIPromptShape`, :81-84). That mode uses `@Generable OnDevicePlaylistSelection { songIds: [String] }` (:31-34, :73-78), with no maximumCount guide.
- Token count is estimated as chars/4 (:42-44).
- Errors are mapped only when they are `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError` (:37-39, :55-70). [NEW] The iOS 27 SDK deprecates `GenerationError` in favour of `LanguageModelError`, `SystemLanguageModel.Error` and `LanguageModelSession.Error`, all iOS 27.0. If Hoa's iOS 27 phone throws the new types, they skip this catch, reach `AiProviderSupport.wrap`, and come out as raw text with the "Offline" prefix.

Status and settings:
- `AIProviderStatus` (App/Services/AI/AIProviderStatus.swift:25-32, check at :61-67) caches whether a provider is set up. [FIX] `refresh` (:40-57) is main-actor isolated; only `check` is `@concurrent`. Library's "With AI" entry is gated by it (LibraryView.swift:505). Its disabled state says "Requires an AI provider key…" with a "Set up API key" button (App/Features/Library/LibrarySheets.swift:705-722).
- **Settings › AI features** (App/Features/Settings/Categories/AISettingsSection.swift):
  - provider picker with "Google Gemini (Free)" (:35-41) and Save-on-usage (:42-45);
  - API key (:47-58), model (:59-63) and base URL (:64-78);
  - on-device row (:79-83, `OnDeviceModelRow` :416-446);
  - Advanced block with temperature, topP, topK, max tokens, penalties, sample size and digest (:180-212).

WHY ON-DEVICE MOSTLY FAILS FOR PLAYLISTS TODAY (estimate, not measured on a phone):
- The on-device context window is 4,096 tokens, shared by instructions, prompt, schema and output. Verified: exceededContextWindowSize doc; WWDC26 session 8121.
- The playlist system prompt is about 1,950 characters, roughly 500-550 tokens. I measured the templates: playlist layer ≈ 986 + few-shot 301 + universal constraints 471 + persona.
- The prompt also carries the digest (up to ~4,000 characters in safe mode, 32,000 in full: AiPlaylist.swift:63-64, :110-145).
- It also carries a JSON pool of 40 songs (80 with "save on usage" off) (AiPlaylist.swift:197-220).
- iOS song ids are long paths, `f:<rootID>/<relative path>` (App/Library/LibraryFiles.swift:22-26), and they appear in the digest, the pool and the output.
- For a library imported from folders, the prompt alone is likely around 3,500-4,000+ tokens.
- The 3B model also has to copy 40-70-character path ids exactly, or the songs are dropped (`AiPlaylistPrompt.playlist`, :273-281).
- [FIX] The model may return ids from the pool or from the digest's LISTENED and DISCOVERY lines (the mapping uses allSongs + pool: :276). So about 40 pool songs plus up to ~45 digest ids are reachable in safe mode. Lab requests of 50-150 songs can't realistically be met within 4k tokens anyway.
- Translation output is twice the input, so long songs, and CJK or Vietnamese lyrics (about 1 token per character, per Apple's context-window article), overflow too. Explicit lyrics can also trip the default guardrails.

recommendedPlan.change:
Ask Hoa which iPhone model he has and whether Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri is on.
- The on-device model only exists on Apple Intelligence iPhones: iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max, and iPhone 16 or later (iPhone Air included) (support.apple.com/en-us/121115).
- iPhone 13 Pro and 14 Pro are 120 Hz but NOT eligible.
- The answer decides whether the Core ML fallback (Phase 2) is needed at all.
- He can also read Settings › AI features › On-Device Model on his current build (AISettingsSection.swift:416-446). Ask whether he has seen "No Internet Connection" from the AI playlist sheet while online: that is the on-device misreport described above.

1) Fix the "No Internet Connection" misreport.
- In `error(_:)` (:50-53), pass a provider name without network words, e.g. `providerName: "On-device model"`, instead of `AiProvider.onDevice.displayName`.
- Do NOT change `displayName` itself: it is golden-tested at Packages/PixlCore/Tests/PixlNetTests/AiTests.swift:54.
- Keep every on-device message free of "network", "connect", "offline", "wifi", "timeout", "key" and "config". These words are matched by AiPlaylist.swift:289-291, AIPlaylistController.swift:250-253 and AILyricsTranslator.swift:73.
- Update the :58 message: it advises "Save on usage", which the curator makes irrelevant.

2) Catch every error, not just `GenerationError` (:37-39). Map it with `OnDeviceModel.failure(for:)` (next steps), which checks GenerationError (26.x) first and then the iOS 27 types through Compat27.

3) String requests use the permissive-guardrails model (:27), via `LanguageModelSession(model: OnDeviceModel.permissive, instructions:)`.

4) The JSON-array mapping (:31-34) uses `.greedy`. Add `@Guide(.maximumCount(…))` or clamp in Swift.

5) Cap `maximumResponseTokens` to (contextSize − estimated input), not 4096.

6) `countTokens` (:42-44) delegates to `OnDeviceModel`.

Keep the generic orchestrator path for cloud-fallback mode and future prompt types. `AIPromptShape` (:81-112) stays for the demo client.

Add the iOS 27 error mapping. CI only allows iOS 27 availability checks in this file (ci/check-forbidden.sh §6).
- Add `import FoundationModels`, which is allowed by ci/check-forbidden.sh:20.
- Add `nonisolated static func onDeviceFailure(_ error: any Error) -> OnDeviceFailure?` on `Compat27`. Mark it `nonisolated`, because the enum is MainActor by default isolation.
- Body: `#if compiler(>=6.4)` → `if #available(iOS 27, *)`, then:
  - `LanguageModelError`: `.contextSizeExceeded` → .tooLong; `.guardrailViolation` and `.refusal` → .blocked; `.unsupportedLanguageOrLocale` → .language; `.rateLimited` → .busy; `.timeout` → .slow; `default` → .other (the enum is `@nonexhaustive`).
  - `LanguageModelSession.Error.concurrentRequests` → .busy.
  - `SystemLanguageModel.Error.assetsUnavailable` → .notReady.
  - `#else` / fallback: return nil.
- `OnDeviceFailure` is a `nonisolated enum` that lives in OnDeviceModel.swift.
- Verify on BOTH the xcode-27 lane and the fallback-xcode26 lane. Coordinate merges: other workstreams in this batch (Liquid Glass, accent colour) are likely to edit Compat27.swift too.

Add a `providerChain: (@Sendable (AiProvider) async -> [AiProvider])? = nil` parameter to `AiOrchestrator.init` (:208-223).
- Store it non-optional, defaulting to `{ AiProviderSupport.buildProviderChain($0) }`.
- Use it at :249: `for provider in await providerChain(userProvider)`.
- Do NOT change `buildProviderChain` or `AiProvider.fromString`: they are Android-exact and golden-tested (AiTests.swift:10-13, :51; NetGoldenTests.swift:109-113). Package.swift needs no edit, and PixlCore stays dependency-free and Windows-buildable.
- Add a Swift Testing case to Packages/PixlCore/Tests/PixlNetTests/AiTests.swift: with a custom `[.onDevice]` chain and no onDeviceClient, a failure lists only ON_DEVICE and the FixtureHTTPClient is never called.

1) Change the `AISettings` default provider from "GEMINI" to "ON_DEVICE" (SettingsStore.swift:618). Installs that never stored a value pick it up automatically. The UI-test suite `pixlaudio.uitest` (AppEnvironment.swift:198) will also default to ON_DEVICE, which changes the AI-category screenshots.
2) Add `cloudFallback: Bool` with a new key `PreferenceKeys.aiCloudFallback = "ai_cloud_fallback"` beside :111-117, default false. It is only needed if Hoa keeps cloud providers.
3) Add `sync(\.cloudFallback, self, f)` to `reload(from f: AISettings)` (SettingsReload.swift:125-137). Otherwise a restore leaves the in-memory value stale.
4) Add a one-shot key `ai_provider_migrated_v1` for the migration below.

- Make `selectedProvider()` (:22-24) default to `.onDevice` when unset.
- Add `cloudFallbackEnabled()` and `providerChain(_ primary:) async -> [AiProvider]`, which returns `[.onDevice]` when the primary is .onDevice and fallback is off, else `AiProviderSupport.buildProviderChain(primary)`. The bridge is already `@unchecked Sendable` and reads UserDefaults.
- Migration [FIX threading]: `AIProviderStatus.refresh` is main-actor; only `check` (:61-67) is `@concurrent`.
  - Add `@concurrent nonisolated static func needsOnDeviceMigration(storedProvider: String) async -> Bool`. It returns true if the stored provider is GEMINI and `AISettingsBridge.storedKey(for: .gemini)` is empty. That Keychain read is IPC, so it runs off the main actor.
  - Then, on the main actor, set `env.settings.ai.provider = AiProvider.onDevice.rawValue`. Its didSet persists the value. Do not write UserDefaults behind the store, or the in-memory `AISettings.provider` goes stale.
  - Set the one-shot flag, so a user who later deliberately picks Gemini before pasting a key isn't flipped back on the next launch.
  - Call it as `AIProviderStatus.migrateDefaultProviderIfNeeded(env)` before `refresh` at AppEnvironment.swift:248 (launch), and in the `backup.onRestored` closure (:235-240) before its refresh, ignoring the flag there.
- [FIX] SettingsBackup.swift:24 only shows that `ai_provider` is a restorable string. A restore brings back whatever value the backup holds, possibly GEMINI from an Android backup, so the after-restore re-run is still right.

- Construct the concrete `AISettingsBridge` once and pass `providerChain: { @Sendable [bridgeImpl] p in await bridgeImpl.providerChain(p) }` to `AiOrchestrator` (:50-52). Same pattern as the `@Sendable` factory at :49. Do not touch the main-actor `SettingsStore` from the closure.
- Demo/UI-test wiring (:43-49) stays scripted: `DemoAiSettings` is .gemini, so the default chain applies.
- Own a new `OnDeviceAI` actor and expose `prewarm(_ feature:)` as fire-and-forget. It does nothing in demo mode or when the provider isn't ON_DEVICE.
- Add `var usesOnDeviceCurator: Bool { !isDemo && AiProvider.fromString(settings.ai.provider) == .onDevice }`. UI tests must keep the scripted orchestrator path: the `#demo-error` screenshot depends on it (DemoAiClient.swift:18-23).

Shared on-device helpers in a `nonisolated enum OnDeviceModel`:
- **Availability:** availability state plus user-facing messages for deviceNotEligible, appleIntelligenceNotEnabled and modelNotReady, with no vendor names (rule 9: CI greps App/ string literals for "Apple"); `supportsLocale()` (default arg `Locale.current`).
- **Context:** `contextSize` is a non-throwing `Int`, `@backDeployed(before: iOS 26.4)`, so it is usable on 26.1. Treat values ≤ 0 as 4096.
- **Token counting:** `try await SystemLanguageModel.default.tokenCount(for: Instructions(text))` inside `if #available(iOS 26.4, *)`. This is not an iOS 27 API, so it does not belong in Compat27. The documented signature takes `Instructions` and is `async throws`, so wrap the prompt text in `Instructions(_:)`. Otherwise estimate: 1 token per CJK, Thai or Vietnamese scalar, else characters/3.5.
- **Models:** shared `static let` instances (SystemLanguageModel is Sendable): `.default`, and `permissive = SystemLanguageModel(useCase: .general, guardrails: .permissiveContentTransformations)` for String outputs. Permissive mode does not apply to @Generable or schema outputs.
- **Errors:** `nonisolated enum OnDeviceFailure { tooLong, blocked, language, notReady, busy, slow, unavailable, other(String) }`.
  - `failure(for: any Error)` maps the deprecated `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError` cases (moved from OnDeviceAiClient :55-70; they produce deprecation warnings on Xcode 27, which is fine because warnings aren't errors in project.yml), then falls back to `Compat27.onDeviceFailure(_:)`.
  - Each case has a user message.

`actor OnDeviceAI` holds the `LanguageModelSession`s. [FIX] Apple's docs list LanguageModelSession as Sendable (and Observable), so there is nothing to verify there.

The real hazard is actor reentrancy: awaiting `respond` lets a second call into the actor and onto the same session, which throws concurrentRequests. The chat composer allows that today (TaisChatSheet.swift:206).
- Serialize per session with a `private var tail: Task<Void, Never>?` chain.
- Use separate sessions for chat, intro, greeting and playlist.
- Mark nested types (`Feature`) as `nonisolated enum … : Sendable`.

Pieces:
- **Prewarm:** `prewarm(.playlist / .chat)` creates the session with STATIC instructions and calls `prewarm(promptPrefix:)`; the next request reuses that session. Instructions are fixed when a session is created, so per-request data (taste summary, pool) must go in the prompt.
- **Chat:** `chat(_:)` is multi-turn with short instructions of about 120 tokens (a condensed taizoChatLayer plus the user's persona). On a .tooLong failure, rebuild the session via `init(model:tools:transcript:)` with the last 2 turns, or plain re-instructions, and retry once.
  - Optional: a `LibraryLookupTool: Tool` (artist/genre/album search over `library.songs`), so answers about the user's music are grounded.
  - Optional: `streamResponse` for the text bubble.
  - Strip leaked JSON or reasoning from String replies (iOS 27 beta 4 known issue, forum thread 840236).
- **Intro and greeting:** `introLine(prompt:count:)` and `greeting(...)` both use permissive String output and greedy sampling.

An on-device playlist and Daily Mix curator, used when `AIService.usesOnDeviceCurator`. Make it a `nonisolated struct: Sendable`. Its heavy entry points are `@concurrent`: under approachable concurrency a plain nonisolated async function would run the prompt building on the main actor (handoff §8).

(a) **Request-aware pool:** run `TaisIntentParser.parse(prompt)` (genres, moods, free text). Then reuse `TaisMediaRouter.routeOffline` (TaisDjEngine.swift:141-158) and `SearchIndex` matches, merged with the `DailyMix.personalizedPicks` candidates (AIPlaylistController.computeContext :199-228).

(b) **Compact prompt:** a 3-line taste summary (top genres, artists, phase; no ids) plus a numbered pool, one line per song: `12. Title — Artist · genre · ♥ · 5 plays`. The numbers are aliases, so no path ids ever reach the model.

(c) **Guided output:** prefer an OBJECT root, because a bare array root is unproven:
- `DynamicGenerationSchema(name: "Picks", description: nil, properties: [.init(name: "picks", description: nil, schema: DynamicGenerationSchema(arrayOf: DynamicGenerationSchema(type: Int.self, guides: [.range(1...n)]), minimumElements: min, maximumElements: max), isOptional: false)])`
- → `try GenerationSchema(root:dependencies: [])` → `session.respond(to:schema:options:)` with `GenerationOptions(sampling: .greedy, …)` → `response.content.value([Int].self, forProperty: "picks")`.
- The Int overload of `.range` is not shown explicitly in the docs (only the collapsed `range(_:)` group, with a Decimal example), so prove it on CI first. Fallback: a static `@Generable struct Picks { @Guide(.maximumCount(150)) var picks: [Int] }`, clamped in Swift.

(d) **Budget ladder:** count tokens; shrink the pool by 25% until instructions + pool + schema + output reserve (max × 3 + 40) fit inside contextSize. On .tooLong, retry once with half the pool. On .blocked, retry once asking for a plain String of comma-separated numbers on the permissive model and parse it in Swift.

(e) **Map back:** indices → songs, dedupe, then top up from the prefiltered pool to reach the minimum.

(f) **Long playlists:** if max > what fits (Lab allows up to 150), first ask for a `@Generable PlaylistPlan { genres, artists, moods, energy 1-5, familiar: Bool }` (genres and artists constrained with `.anyOf` to the library's top values). Then fill the playlist deterministically and use the model only to order the first ~40 (owner decision).

Returns `Result<[Song], AiPlaylistGenerationError>` like the existing generator, with messages from `OnDeviceFailure`. It is not used in UI tests. Unit tests inject a chooser closure; for scripted behaviour mirror DemoAiClient.swift:24-29 (every other candidate). [FIX: the previous plan cited :145-150, but the file is 51 lines.]

recommendedPlan.file: Phase 2, only if Hoa's iPhone is not eligible and he wants generative features there: ci/ml/convert_llm.py (new), ci/ml/requirements-llm.txt (new), .github/workflows/ml-convert.yml, App/Services/ML/ModelCatalog.swift, App/Services/AI/CoreMLLanguageModel.swift (new), THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

risks: Hoa's iPhone may not support Apple Intelligence. iPhone 13 Pro and 14 Pro are 120 Hz but not eligible. If so, Phase 1 does nothing on his phone and only Phase 2 (XL) or the deterministic fallbacks help. Even on an eligible phone, the model needs Apple Intelligence turned on, the model downloaded (`modelNotReady`), and the device language set to a supported one (Vietnamese is listed on support.apple.com/en-us/121115 for iOS 27).

iOS 27 error types: the 27 SDK deprecates `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError`. In its place come `LanguageModelError` (contextSizeExceeded, guardrailViolation, refusal, rateLimited, timeout, unsupportedLanguageOrLocale…), `SystemLanguageModel.Error.assetsUnavailable` and `LanguageModelSession.Error.concurrentRequests`, all iOS 27.0. Which type an Xcode-27-built app targeting 26.1 receives on iOS 27 isn't documented. Handle both, the new ones only through Compat27.swift, or the budget ladder's too-long retry and every error message silently stop working on Hoa's phone. Unverified until it runs on his phone.

iOS 27 model quality: Apple acknowledged iOS 27 beta 4 model problems: phantom tool calls, JSON or reasoning leaking into String replies, refusals without instructions (developer.apple.com/forums/thread/840236). The workarounds were @Generable outputs and an explicit 'do not call tools' line. Prefer guided generation for structured output, always pass instructions, and sanitise String replies. Re-check on the iOS 27 release Hoa runs.

The 4,096-token shared context window is the same on iOS 26 and 27 (Apple docs; WWDC26 session 8121). Today's playlist prompt with `f:` path ids very likely overflows. The size estimates are mine; nobody has measured them on a device. Use `tokenCount(for:)` (26.4+) at runtime and keep the shrink-and-retry ladder.

Guardrails: song titles or lyrics with explicit words can trigger a guardrail violation. `.permissiveContentTransformations` only covers String outputs, not @Generable or DynamicGenerationSchema. Mitigation: on a violation, retry the playlist pick as a plain String list of numbers parsed in Swift.

Quality: a ~3B model with 2-4-bit weights has limited world knowledge and reasoning (Apple lists reasoning and math as tasks to avoid). Taizo's free-form music trivia may invent facts; ground answers with a library tool and keep replies short. Model versions differ between 26.0-26.3, 26.4 and 27.0, so prompts may need per-version tuning.

Latency: a cold first call can exceed Taizo's 1.2 s intro budget (TaisDjEngine.swift:37). Apple's 2024 figures: ~0.6 ms per prompt token and ~30 tok/s on iPhone 15 Pro; current models differ. Without prewarm and an asynchronous intro, most intros will be silently dropped.

Concurrency: actor reentrancy means `actor OnDeviceAI` alone does NOT serialize requests. Awaiting `respond` lets a second call reach the same session, which throws concurrentRequests. The chat composer allows sending while a reply is in flight (TaisChatSheet.swift:206). Serialize per session and keep intro, chat and playlist on separate sessions. Background use is rate-limited.

Seams and merges:
- Compat27.swift is shared with the other iOS 27 work in this batch, so expect conflicts.
- LyricsMoreSheet and LyricsView are also touched by the lyrics-page items (static/synced buttons, keep screen on, Liquid Glass).
- LibrarySheets.swift belongs to the Library seam.
Coordinate merges.

UI tests: changing the AISettings default changes the UI-test suite's default too. The AI-category screenshots change (credentials hidden, on-device row shown, probably 'Not available' on the CI simulator). The curator and the asynchronous intro must stay off the demo path, or the AI and Taizo screenshots and the #demo-error screenshot break.

CI simulators almost certainly have no system language model, so on-device code paths can't be screenshot-tested. UI tests must keep the scripted DemoAiClient path, and real verification needs Hoa's phone.

PixlNet's Android-exact behaviour and golden tests (AiTests.swift, NetGoldenTests.swift) break if `buildProviderChain`, `fromString` or `AiProvider.displayName` are edited. Change only through the new optional orchestrator parameter and app-side labels.

A settings restore from an Android backup can bring back ai_provider=GEMINI. Rerun the migration after a restore, from AppEnvironment's `backup.onRestored` (AppEnvironment.swift:235-240), not BackupService. If the user's key was restored too, the migration correctly leaves Gemini.
Translation `.highFidelity` needs iOS 26.4. Older 26.x falls back to the existing configuration. On devices without Apple Intelligence the system may show its language-download prompt.

The DynamicGenerationSchema details are unproven: Int `.range` overload, object root versus array root, and `GeneratedContent.value(_:forProperty:)` for `[Int]`. Prove them in a small CI change first (AGENTS 'never guess signatures'). The static @Generable fallback is the safety net.

Phase 2 risks: memory (Qwen3-0.6B int4 is ~0.35-0.4 GB of weights plus ~0.23 GB KV cache at 2k context in fp16, on top of the audio engine), tokenizer correctness, conversion parity, ~400 MB-1 GB downloads, and many CI rounds.
ownerDecisions: Which iPhone model do you have, and does Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri show it as on? (A: iPhone 15 Pro or newer → on-device model works; build Phase 1 only. B: older 120 Hz Pro, i.e. 13 Pro or 14 Pro → no system model; decide on Phase 2.)

What should happen to the cloud AI providers (Gemini, OpenAI, Groq, Ollama…)? (A, suggested: keep them as an optional 'Cloud assistants' section, off by default, with no automatic fallback to the cloud. B: remove them from the app's settings entirely, so it is fully local. C: keep today's behaviour, with on-device as the default but still falling back to any cloud provider that has a key.)

On iPhones without Apple Intelligence, what should AI features do? (A, suggested: no language model. Playlists come from a smart offline mix built from your library, translation uses the system translator, and Taizo answers play/queue/find but not general questions. B: download a ~400 MB-1 GB open-source model (Qwen, Apache-2.0) converted to Core ML; a large job, many CI rounds. C: wait.)
Lyrics: merge 'Translate via AI' and 'Translate on device' into one 'Translate' button that uses the system translator's high-quality AI mode (suggested), or keep both buttons?

AI Playlist Lab asks for up to 150 songs, but the on-device model can only consider about 40-150 songs at once. (A, suggested: the model reads your request and picks genres, artists, mood and energy; the app then fills the playlist from your library and the model orders the first ~40. B: cap on-device playlists at what fits, about 40 songs.)
Port Android's AI home greeting (a one-line greeting plus 2-3 sentence insight, generated once a day on-device)? (Suggested: yes; it's small and cheap.)

Taizo chat: let it answer general music questions with the on-device model (it can sometimes get facts wrong), add a 'look up my library' tool so it answers about your own music accurately, and make it remember the conversation? (Suggested: yes to all three; or restrict it to questions about your library.)
If you had picked Gemini before and never added a key, switch you to on-device automatically, once? (Suggested: yes.)
Hide the advanced AI knobs (Top P/K, penalties, max tokens, sample size, digest, Save on usage) when on-device is selected, keeping only Temperature? (Suggested: yes.)

options.name: A. Foundation Models on-device by default plus typed per-feature on-device paths (recommended Phase 1)
options.description:
System language model for all features:
- **Playlists:** a compact, index-aliased playlist curator.
- **Chat and greeting:** prewarmed, serialized multi-turn chat and greeting.
- **Translation:** the Translation framework's `.highFidelity` strategy.
- **Errors:** the 'Offline' misreport fixed; iOS 26 and iOS 27 error types both mapped.
- **Cloud:** providers optional (or removed), with no automatic cloud fallback.
options.pros: Apple framework only, already linked and CI-proven (OnDeviceAiClient). No download, no key, private and offline. Fixes the context-overflow problem and the 'No Internet Connection' misreport. Translation becomes reliable and works on non-AI devices too (lowLatency fallback). Effort L.
options.cons: Only on Apple Intelligence iPhones with the feature on. 4,096-token budget. Small-model quality limits for trivia. iOS 27 error-type behaviour unproven until it runs on Hoa's phone. Can't be screenshot-tested on CI.

options.name: B. Minimal: only switch the default provider to ON_DEVICE
options.description: Change the defaults (SettingsStore.swift:618, AISettingsBridge.swift:23), stop the cloud chain and fix the OnDeviceAiClient error provider name; leave prompts as they are.
options.pros: Effort S; a few lines. Fixes the misleading 'No Internet Connection' errors.
options.cons: Playlist and Daily Mix prompts with path ids will likely overflow 4,096 tokens or return non-matching ids. Translation overflows on long or CJK songs and trips guardrails on explicit lyrics. Intro lines time out. Looks broken to Hoa.

options.name: C. Phase 2 fallback: Core ML small LLM (Qwen3-0.6B / Qwen2.5-0.5B-1.5B, Apache-2.0) converted on CI
options.description: Same pipeline as wav2vec2/MDX (ml-convert.yml → models-v1 → ModelManager). Stateful KV cache plus int4. Our own Swift BPE tokenizer, ChatML template and sampler, exposed as an `AiClient`.
options.pros: Works on any iOS 26 device. Weights are data and inference is Core ML, so it fits rule 2. Reuses the existing download and SHA-pin machinery.
options.cons: XL effort: tokenizer, conversion parity, memory and many CI rounds. 0.4-1 GB download. Weak quality at 0.5-1.5B, so suitable for picks, intros and greetings, not translation or trivia. Qwen3 needs a separate transformers pin.

options.name: D. Core AI (iOS 27) with an exported open model
options.description: Export with Apple's coreai-models recipes on CI (build-time Python is fine). Run it via the Core AI framework, ideally through FoundationModels' `LanguageModel` protocol (CoreAILanguageModel).
options.pros: Apple's newest path. Same LanguageModelSession API as the system model.
options.cons: The coreai-models package depends on swift-transformers, xgrammar and hummingbird (verified in its Package.swift; Jinja comes in through swift-transformers), which breaks rule 2. Without it we write our own executor and tokenizer (XL). iOS 27-only (Compat27, fallback-xcode26 lane, `CoreAI` missing from the ci/check-forbidden.sh import allowlist). Ahead-of-time compile only for A17 Pro or later, the same devices that already have the system model, so it doesn't help the non-AI case.

options.name: E. Private Cloud Compute model (iOS 27, 32K context) or custom adapters
options.pros: PCC: larger context (32K) and reasoning, no API key.
options.cons: Not viable. PCC isn't local, and it requires a managed entitlement with eligibility requirements (PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel doc page), which free-Apple-ID sideloading can't get. Adapters need the managed `com.apple.developer.foundation-model-adapter` entitlement, take ~160 MB each, and the toolkit's last release (26.0.0) is 'not compatible with … iOS … 27 and later' (adapter page, verified).

research:
Sources are developer.apple.com unless noted. Doc JSON was read via developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/…; this reviewer re-fetched the pages marked [verified].

**On-device model: context window and limits**
- [verified] 4,096 tokens per session, shared by instructions, prompts, tools, schemas and output. About 3-4 characters per token in Latin languages, about 1 per character in Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Vietnamese (documentation/foundationmodels/managing-the-context-window; documentation/foundationmodels/languagemodelsession/generationerror/exceededcontextwindowsize(_:)).
- [verified] WWDC26 'Coding Intelligence, Machine Learning & AI Group Lab' (videos/play/wwdc2026/8121/): \"It's 4096 and it is a shared window … PCC is 32 K.\"
- [verified] `contextSize`: iOS 26.0, `@backDeployed(before: iOS 26.4)`, `final var contextSize: Int` (documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/contextsize).
- [verified] `tokenCount(for:)`: iOS 26.4, `nonisolated(nonsending) final func tokenCount(for instructions: Instructions) async throws -> Int` (documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/tokencount(for:)). `Instructions` has `init(_:)`.
- [verified] Three model versions: 26.0-26.3, 26.4 and 27.0 (documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel).
- iOS 27 `SystemLanguageModel.variant` (`.core3`, `.coreAdvanced3`): documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/variant-swift.struct.

**iOS 27 error types (NEW)**
- [verified] documentation/updates/foundationmodels (June 2026): \"Use the improved error types, like LanguageModelError … SystemLanguageModel/Error … LanguageModelSession/Error\".
- [verified] `LanguageModelSession.GenerationError` and all its cases are deprecated in iOS 27.0, e.g. exceededContextWindowSize: \"Use LanguageModelError/contextSizeExceeded(_:) instead\".
- [verified] `LanguageModelError` (iOS 27.0, `@nonexhaustive`): contextSizeExceeded, rateLimited, refusal, timeout, guardrailViolation, unsupportedCapability, unsupportedTranscriptContent, unsupportedGenerationGuide, unsupportedLanguageOrLocale (documentation/foundationmodels/languagemodelerror).
- [verified] `LanguageModelSession.Error` (27.0): concurrentRequests, transcriptMutationWhileResponding.
- [verified] `SystemLanguageModel.Error` (27.0): assetsUnavailable.
- [verified] iOS 27 beta 4 model issues and Apple's workarounds: developer.apple.com/forums/thread/840236.

**Availability, languages and guardrails**
- Availability reasons: appleIntelligenceNotEnabled, deviceNotEligible, modelNotReady (documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/availability-swift.enum/unavailablereason).
- [verified] `final func supportsLocale(_ locale: Locale = Locale.current) -> Bool`, 26.0; prefer it over supportedLanguages (documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/supportslocale(_:)).
- [verified] `.permissiveContentTransformations` (26.0): String responses won't throw guardrailViolation; non-String responses behave like default (documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/guardrails/permissivecontenttransformations).
- [verified] `convenience init(useCase:guardrails:)`; UseCase `.general` / `.contentTagging`.

**Sessions, structured output and tools**
- [verified] `LanguageModelSession` is a `final class` that conforms to Sendable and Observable (documentation/foundationmodels/languagemodelsession). It has init(model:tools:instructions:), init(model:tools:transcript:), isResponding, streamResponse, prewarm.
- [verified] `final func prewarm(promptPrefix: Prompt? = nil)`; only use it with at least 1 second before the respond call.
- [verified] `respond(to:schema:includeSchemaInPrompt:options:) -> Response<GeneratedContent>`.
- [verified] `DynamicGenerationSchema`: init(arrayOf:minimumElements:maximumElements:), init(name:description:properties:), init<Value>(type:guides:), and `Property(name:description:schema:isOptional:)`.
- [verified] `GenerationSchema(root:dependencies:) throws`.
- [verified] `GeneratedContent.value(_:)` and `value(_:forProperty:)`.
- [verified] `GenerationOptions.SamplingMode.greedy`.
- GenerationGuide `range(_:)`: the docs show a Decimal overload and a collapsed group. The Int overload is likely but must be proven on CI. `maximumCount<Element>(Int)` is [verified].
- Prompting guidance: concise prompts of at most 3 paragraphs, ask for less content (managing-the-context-window; prompting-an-on-device-foundation-model).

**Performance and devices**
- About 3B parameters at ~3.7 bits per weight; 0.6 ms per prompt token time-to-first-token and 30 tok/s on iPhone 15 Pro. These are 2024 model figures (machinelearning.apple.com/research/introducing-apple-foundation-models).
- [verified] Eligible devices: iPhone 16 models or later, iPhone 15 Pro and Pro Max. Vietnamese is in the iOS 27 language list (support.apple.com/en-us/121115).

**Translation framework**
- [verified] `TranslationSession.Strategy` (iOS 26.4): `.highFidelity` \"uses Apple Intelligence … On devices without Apple Intelligence, it falls back to the traditional models used by lowLatency\"; no extra language download when Apple Intelligence is on.
- [verified] `Configuration(source:target:preferredStrategy:)` (iOS 26.4).
- Docs: documentation/translation/translationsession/strategy and …/strategy/highfidelity.

**iOS 27 options that don't fit**
- [verified] PCC: `PrivateCloudComputeLanguageModel` (iOS 27, contextSize, quotaUsage) requires a managed entitlement with eligibility requirements (documentation/foundationmodels/privatecloudcomputelanguagemodel). The earlier '2M downloads' detail was not re-verified and is dropped.
- [verified] coreai-models' Package.swift depends on swift-argument-parser, huggingface/swift-transformers, mlc-ai/xgrammar and hummingbird (raw.githubusercontent.com/apple/coreai-models/main/Package.swift), so it breaks rule 2.
- Core AI ahead-of-time compile supports only A17 Pro or later (documentation/coreai/compiling-core-ai-models-ahead-of-time; not re-checked).
- [verified] Adapters: entitlement `com.apple.developer.foundation-model-adapter`, ~160 MB each; \"Version 26.0.0 is the last release of this toolkit and is not compatible with … iOS … 27 and later\" (developer.apple.com/apple-intelligence/foundation-models-adapter/).

**Core ML fallback (Phase 2)**
- `MLState` / `makeState()` / `prediction(from:using:)` (iOS 18): documentation/coreml/mlstate.
- coremltools stateful models: apple.github.io/coremltools/docs-guides/source/stateful-models.html.
- Apple's Llama 3.1 Core ML recipe: machinelearning.apple.com/research/core-ml-on-device-llama.
- Third-party data point: soniqo.audio/guides/chat.

**Model licences**
- Qwen3-0.6B and Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B-Instruct: Apache-2.0 (huggingface.co/Qwen).
- Llama 3.2 and Gemma 3 are use-restricted, so avoid them.
newAppleAPIs: SystemLanguageModel.tokenCount(for: Instructions) async throws -> Int + Instructions.init(_:) — iOS 26.4 (guard with #available(iOS 26.4, *)) — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/tokencount(for:)
Tool protocol (name, description, Arguments, call(arguments:)) — iOS 26.0 — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/tool
GenerationGuide .range(_:) (Int overload to prove on CI), .maximumCount(_:), .anyOf(_:) — iOS 26.0 — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/generationguide

(Optional, iOS 27, Compat27 only) SystemLanguageModel.variant / Variant.core3 / .coreAdvanced3 — iOS 27.0 — https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundationmodels/systemlanguagemodel/variant-swift.struct
alternativeCauses: Hoa may already have hit the on-device model without knowing it. With the default Gemini and no key, the provider chain ends at ON_DEVICE (AiProvider.swift:142-148; the Daily Mix sparkle is ungated, MixScreens.swift:200-205). Every on-device failure then shows as 'No Internet Connection' because the provider name 'On-Device (Offline)' matches the 'offline' rule (AiPlaylist.swift:290-291, AIPlaylistController.swift:252-253). Any 'AI doesn't work / says no internet' report is most likely this.

The on-device path may already fail on Hoa's phone for reasons that have nothing to do with prompts: the device is not eligible, Apple Intelligence is off, the model is not yet downloaded, or the language is unsupported. Check Settings › AI features › On-Device Model and Developer › Diagnostics (DiagnosticsModel.swift:58) on his current build first.

On iOS 27 the framework may throw the new LanguageModelError / SystemLanguageModel.Error types. OnDeviceAiClient's `catch let error as LanguageModelSession.GenerationError` (:37) would then miss them, so errors surface as raw type descriptions with the 'Offline' prefix, not as the mapped messages.

If his library comes from the Music app (`mp:` ids, about 22 characters) rather than folders (`f:` path ids), today's on-device playlist prompt may just fit at about 3,000 tokens. Then the overflow is mainly a problem for folder imports, 'save on usage' off, or 'Full' digest mode.
